Ingredients:

  • 80 g rolled oats

  • 120 ml apple juice (or half apple juice, half milk)

  • 2 tbsp grated apple

  • 1 tbsp chia seeds

  • 1 tbsp goji berries

  • Pinch cinnamon

  • Pinch salt

  • 1–2 tbsp Greek yoghurt (to fold in before serving)

  • Vanilla

Method:

  1. Mix oats, apple juice, chia, grated apple, cinnamon + salt.

  2. Cover and soak overnight.

  3. In the morning, fold in 1–2 tbsp Greek yoghurt to make it creamy.

  4. Adjust with extra milk/yoghurt if too thick.

Chai-Poached Pear

Ingredients:

  • 4 pears (firm)

  • 500 ml water

  • 250 ml apple juice or white wine (optional)

  • 80 g sugar or honey

  • Peel of 1 lemon

  • 2 chai tea bags or:

    • 1 cinnamon stick

    • 4 cloves

    • 3 cardamom pods

    • 1 star anise

    • Small nub ginger

Method:

  1. Peel pears, halve or quarter, remove core.

  2. Bring liquid, sugar, lemon peel + chai spices to a simmer.

  3. Add pears, cover with a baking paper cartouche.

  4. Poach on low for 12–20 min until just tender.

  5. Cool pears in the liquid for best flavour.

  6. Slice for service.

Yoghurt Component (Dairy)

  • 2–3 large spoonfuls of full-fat Greek yoghurt

  • Optional: a touch of honey or vanilla

  • Optional: fold through lime zest for a modern touch

Plating (Café style)

  1. Spoon bircher base into a bowl.

  2. Add a thick ripple of Greek yoghurt on top.

  3. Fan out chai-poached pear slices.

  4. Finish with:

    • Toasted almonds or pepitas

    • Drizzle of chai syrup from the pot

    • Fresh berries or edible flowers (spring)

    • Sprinkle of cinnamon

🟢 Green Congee Ingredients

Spices & aromatics

  • ½ tsp cumin seeds

  • ½ tsp fennel seeds

  • ½ tsp mustard seeds

  • 1 curry leaf

  • 2 cloves garlic, minced

  • fresh ginger, minced (about 1 tsp)

Congee base

  • ⅓ cup jasmine rice

  • 700 ml water

  • 1 tsp salt

  • ¼ tsp pepper

  • 1 tbsp kelp meal

  • 100 ml coconut milk

Method

1. Cook the congee

  1. Wash the rice well.

  2. Add rice, 700 ml water, salt, pepper and kelp meal to a pot.

  3. Bring to a boil on high heat.

  4. Once boiling, reduce to low heat and simmer for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
    → The rice should break down and become thick, creamy, porridge-like.

. Make the spice base

  1. Heat coconut oil in a pan.

  2. Add cumin, fennel, mustard seeds and the curry leaf.

  3. Fry until fragrant (10–20 seconds).

  4. Add garlic and ginger and cook until golden.

3. Combine spice base to congee

  1. Pour the green purée into the congee.

  2. Stir well and cook together for 5 more minutes.

  3. Taste and adjust with salt, pepper or more coconut milk.

Batch / yield (1×): 5kg raw brisket → about 2.8–3kg cooked, pulled meat (≈ 28 × 100g portions)
Used in: 8hr brisket plate · chilli scramble & hash add-on · sides

Ingredients

  • 5 kg beef brisket, point end, fat cap trimmed to 5 mm
  • Dry rub: 60 g flaky salt
  • 30 g coarse black pepper
  • 30 g smoked paprika
  • 20 g garlic powder
  • 20 g onion powder
  • 40 g brown sugar
  • 10 g ground cumin
  • 5 g chilli flakes
  • Braise: 2 brown onions, sliced
  • 6 garlic cloves, crushed
  • 500 ml beef stock
  • 250 ml red wine
  • 60 ml red wine vinegar
  • 40 ml tamari
  • 2 bay leaves

Method

  1. Day 1 – marinate: mix the rub. Pat brisket dry, rub all over (use all of it). Wrap tightly and refrigerate 12–24 hours.
  2. Day 2 – oven to 140°C (combi: 140°C, 30% steam if available). Sear brisket fat-side down in a large tray on the stove until well browned, 4–5 min each side.
  3. Scatter onion and garlic under the meat in a deep gastronorm. Mix stock, wine, vinegar and tamari; pour around (not over) the brisket to come 2 cm up the side. Add bay.
  4. Cover tightly with baking paper then foil. Cook 7½–8 hours until a probe slides in with no resistance (core about 95°C).
  5. Rest covered 45 minutes. Lift out, strain the braising liquid into a jug and skim off the fat (keep the fat for the polenta chips).
  6. Pull the meat with two forks, discarding large fat pockets. Toss with 250–300 ml of the reduced braising liquid so it's glossy and moist; taste and adjust salt.
  7. Portion 100 g into vac bags or labelled containers. Chill fast (below 5°C within 4 hours). Keeps 4 days chilled or 2 months frozen.
  8. To serve: reheat portions with a splash of braising liquid in a covered pan or in the combi until 75°C+ in the centre.

Notes

Reduce leftover braising liquid by half for the jus on the brisket plate. Brisket is seed-oil free; sear in beef fat or olive oil.

Allergens & dietaries

Gluten free if tamari is GF. Dairy free.

Ingredients

  • 260 g apple, peeled, 7 mm dice (about 2 large)
  • 115 g butter, melted
  • 200 g brown sugar
  • 165 ml milk
  • 1 large egg
  • 5 ml white vinegar
  • 300 g wholemeal flour (or plain)
  • 5 g bicarb soda
  • 4 g cinnamon (Icaro: doubled)
  • pinch salt
  • Topping: 25 g raw / demerara sugar
  • Optional crumble: 50 g flour + 50 g brown sugar + 40 g butter + 2 g cinnamon, rubbed together

Method

  1. Oven 200°C. Butter or line a 12-hole muffin tin.
  2. Whisk melted butter and brown sugar, then the milk, egg and vinegar.
  3. Scatter the flour, bicarb, cinnamon and salt over the batter and whisk about 10 strokes, just until combined.
  4. Stir in the apple with as few strokes as possible.
  5. Fill cases to the top, sprinkle with raw sugar or crumble. Put in the oven and drop to 180°C.
  6. Bake 20 minutes (18 fan) until a skewer comes out clean. Rest 5 minutes, then cool on a rack.

Notes

Adds a 4th muffin flavour — great autumn/winter rotation. Freezes well; refresh 5 minutes at 160°C.

Allergens & dietaries

Gluten, dairy, egg.

Ingredients

  • 440 g tin crushed pineapple, drained (keep 65 ml juice)
  • 185 ml milk
  • 5 ml white vinegar

  • 265 g brown sugar
  • 125 ml light olive oil (Icaro swap for vegetable oil)

Ingredients

  • 225 g unsalted butter, browned
  • 300 g plain flour
  • 9 g cornflour
  • 1 g baking powder (¼ tsp)
  • 2.5 g bicarb soda (½ tsp)
  • 3 g salt
  • 220 g brown sugar
  • 110 g caster sugar
  • 1 egg
  • 1 egg yolk
  • 5 ml vanilla
  • 250 g dark chocolate chips (+ extra to press on top)
  • 150 g milk chocolate chips

Method

  1. Brown the butter until it smells nutty and has golden specks; pour into a bowl and cool to room temperature (about 45 min).
  2. Whisk the flour, cornflour, baking powder, bicarb and salt.
  3. Stir both sugars into the cooled butter, then the egg, yolk and vanilla until glossy.
  4. Mix in the dry ingredients until nearly combined, add both chocolates and finish mixing.
  5. Weigh 155 g balls, press into thick 3.75 cm discs, chill at least 12 hours (up to 48).
  6. Bake from cold at 170°C fan, 4 per tray well spaced, about 17 minutes — edges golden, centre set but pale.
  7. Press extra chips on top straight away; cool 20 minutes on the tray (they finish cooking).

Notes

Café: make a double batch on Friday and keep balls chilled; bake to order through the day so the case always has warm cookies. Brown butter is seed-oil free.

Ingredients

  • 2.5 g bicarb soda
  • pinch salt
  • 125 g butter, melted
  • 165 g caster sugar
  • 165 ml milk
  • 1 egg
  • 10 ml vanilla
  • 5 ml white vinegar
  • Flavour 1 – Raspberry & white choc: 250 g raspberries (frozen OK, don't thaw) + 150 g white choc chips
  • Flavour 2 – Banana, walnut & dark choc: 2 mashed bananas (reduce milk by 60 ml) + 80 g walnuts + 100 g dark chips

  2. Whisk dry ingredients.

  6. Rest 10 minutes in the tin, then cool on a rack.

Rotate: Mon/Wed/Fri raspberry & white choc, Tue/Thu banana walnut, weekends blueberry crumble. Savoury option: cheesy zucchini muffins — https://www.recipetineats.com/cheesy-zucchini-muffins/

Source: RecipeTin Eats (Nagi Maehashi) · See photos ↗
Finished look: Tall, fluffy golden scones split by hand with strawberry jam and whipped cream

Ingredients

  • 450 g self-raising flour
  • 80 g cold salted butter, 1 cm cubes
  • 250 ml cold milk (+ extra to brush)
  • To serve: strawberry jam
  • 250 ml cream whipped with 15 g sugar and 2 ml vanilla

Method

  1. Oven 180°C fan. Line a tray.
  2. Pulse flour and butter in a food processor about 8 seconds to breadcrumbs.
  3. Pour the milk all over and pulse 6–8 seconds until it just clumps.
  4. Tip out, knead no more than 10 times, pat to 3 cm thick.
  5. Cut straight down with a floured 5 cm cutter — never twist. Pack them close on the tray; re-roll scraps once.
  6. Brush tops with milk. Bake 10–12 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding.
  7. Wrap in a tea towel to keep the tops soft. Serve warm with jam and cream.

Notes

Best within 2 hours — bake twice a day. Cheese scones variation: add 100 g grated cheddar + pinch cayenne. Pairs well with the Devonshire-style 'scone + pot of tea' deal.

Allergens & dietaries

Gluten, dairy.

Ingredients

  • 150 g plain flour
  • 6 g baking powder
  • pinch salt
  • 2 eggs, room temperature
  • 165 g caster sugar
  • 60 g butter
  • 125 ml full-cream milk
  • 10 ml vanilla
  • 7 ml light olive oil (Icaro swap)
  • Frosting: vanilla buttercream or Swiss meringue buttercream

Method

  1. Oven 160°C fan (preheat 20 minutes). Line a 12-hole tin.
  2. Whisk flour, baking powder and salt.
  3. Heat milk and butter until the butter melts (don't boil).
  4. Beat eggs 30 seconds, add sugar slowly, then beat 6 minutes until tripled and nearly white.
  5. Fold in the flour in three lots on low speed.
  6. Mix a little batter into the hot milk with vanilla and oil, then beat it back into the batter on low until smooth.
  7. Fill cases two-thirds. Bake 22 minutes. Cool before frosting.

Notes

The whipped-egg method is what keeps them moist for days — don't skip the 6-minute beat.

Gluten, dairy, egg.

Ingredients

  • 600 g oranges (about 2), whole
  • 6 large eggs
  • 275 g white sugar
  • 5 g GF baking powder
  • 275 g almond meal

Method

  1. Cover whole oranges with cold water, boil 10 minutes, drain; repeat twice more (or boil 40 minutes straight).
  2. Cool, slice and dice (remove seeds).
  3. Oven 140°C fan. Line a 23 cm tin.
  4. Blitz oranges in a food processor to a marmalade texture.
  5. Add almond meal, eggs, baking powder and sugar; pulse until combined.
  6. Bake about 60 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
  7. Cool completely in the tin before turning out — it's sticky.

Notes

Boil oranges a day ahead and keep chilled. Lemons don't work (too bitter). Keeps 5 days, improves on day 2. Glaze with orange syrup for shine.

recipes.h:
Sep 19, 2026

Quick reference

Eight drinks, each a single build or a pour from a pre-batched bottle, with no shaking on ice.

DrinkPriceGlassBuild
Mimosa$14FluteProsecco, then orange juice
Aperol Spritz$16Large wine glass, iceProsecco, Aperol, soda
Limoncello Spritz$18Large wine glass, iceLimoncello, prosecco, soda
Paloma Spritz$20Large wine glass, salted rim, iceTequila and grapefruit mix, prosecco
Good Morning Negroni$23Rocks, large cubePour from batch bottle
Irish Coffee$23Rocks or tumbler, iceWhiskey, fig liqueur, honey syrup, cold brew, cream cloud
Sunrise Tonic$18Highball, iceAperol, tonic, cold brew float
Espresso Martini On The Rocks$23Rocks, icePour from batch bottle, cream cloud

Prep and batching

These prep items are made before service so every drink is one pour and a top-up. Label each bottle with the item, the date made and the use-by date.

Prep itemRecipeKeeps
Honey syrup100ml honey + 100ml hot water. Stir until dissolved, cool, bottle.2 weeks, fridge
Vanilla cream cloud700ML pouring cream + vanilla syrup to taste, thin with milk slightly. No whipper: shake in a sealed jar 20 to 30 seconds until just thickened and still pourable.2 days, fridge
Good Morning Negroni batch300ml gin + 250ml Campari + 250ml sweet vermouth + 150ml coffee liqueur + 200ml water. Stir, bottle. Pour 115ml per drink.1 week, fridge
Espresso Martini batch400ml vodka + 300ml coffee liqueur + 400ml cold brew. Stir, bottle. Pour 110ml per drink.3 days, fridge

Paloma mix: combine tequila and pink grapefruit juice at 1 to 2 (for example 300ml tequila + 600ml juice). Pour 90ml per drink, then top with prosecco. Juice fades quickly, so make this fresh each morning.

Vanilla syrup: use a bought one, or make 1:1 sugar syrup and add half a teaspoon of vanilla bean paste per 100ml.

Spritzes and fizz

All five are built directly in the glass, so nobody needs a shaker or strainer. Chill the prosecco, tonic and soda, and pour the fizz last.

DrinkMeasuresMethodGarnish
Mimosa90ml prosecco, 60ml orange juiceTilt the flute. Pour prosecco first, then top with juice so it doesn't foam over.Orange twist (optional)
Aperol Spritz90ml prosecco, 60ml Aperol, 30ml sodaFill the glass with ice. Pour prosecco, then Aperol, then soda. One gentle stir.Orange half-wheel
Limoncello Spritz45ml limoncello, 90ml prosecco, 30ml sodaFill the glass with ice. Pour limoncello, then prosecco, then soda. One gentle stir.Lemon wheel, mint sprig
Paloma Spritz90ml Paloma mix (30ml tequila + 60ml pink grapefruit juice), 60ml proseccoRub a grapefruit wedge round half the rim and dip in salt. Fill with ice. Pour the mix, then top with prosecco.Grapefruit wedge
Sunrise Tonic30ml Aperol, 90ml tonic, 30ml cold brewFill the glass with ice. Pour Aperol, then tonic. Pour cold brew slowly over the back of a bar spoon so it floats. Don't stir.Orange wheel

Rim salt: keep a saucer of fine sea salt at the bar, and add a pinch of chilli flakes if you want a kick on the Paloma.

Stirred and coffee drinks

The Negroni and Espresso Martini pour straight from batch bottles, and the Irish Coffee is the only one built from scratch.

DrinkMeasuresMethodGarnish
Good Morning Negroni115ml from the batch bottle (per serve: 30ml gin, 25ml Campari, 25ml sweet vermouth, 15ml coffee liqueur, 20ml water)Place one large cube in a chilled rocks glass. Pour the batch. No stirring needed.Orange peel, expressed over the top
Irish Coffee30ml Irish whiskey, 15ml fig liqueur, 10ml honey syrup, 90ml cold brew, 30ml vanilla cream cloudFill the glass with ice. Add whiskey, fig liqueur and honey syrup. Top with cold brew and give it one stir. Spoon the cream cloud over the top.Grated nutmeg or cinnamon (optional)
Espresso Martini On The Rocks110ml from the batch bottle (per serve: 40ml vodka, 30ml coffee liqueur, 40ml cold brew), 30ml vanilla cream cloudFill a rocks glass with ice. Pour the batch, then spoon the cream cloud over the top.3 coffee beans on the cloud

Hot Irish Coffee for cold mornings: swap the cold brew for 90ml hot batch brew, and serve it in a heat-proof stemmed glass with no ice.

Service notes

Speed comes from setup, so do this before doors open.

  • Cut garnishes for the morning: orange wheels, orange half-wheels, orange peels, lemon wheels, grapefruit wedges, mint sprigs. Keep them covered in the fridge.

  • Use jiggers marked at 15ml, 30ml and 45ml, and a marked cup for the 60ml, 90ml and 110ml pours.

  • Keep cold brew, prosecco, tonic, soda and both batch bottles in the bar fridge, and the cream whipper on its own shelf.

  • Cream cloud contains dairy, and Irish Coffee contains honey. Tell guests when they ask about allergens.

  • Wipe the salt saucer and swap the salt daily.
